change: in-app updater for the github release channel, two build flavours

covers: manifest parsing of untrusted documents: wrong types, unknown and duplicate ABIs, non-repository download addresses, oversized input
every trust refusal: foreign package, downgrade, replay, older version name, foreign certificate digest, low API level, missing architecture
downloaded APK checks: size, checksum, package, version code, single signer, signer equalling the installed app, native architectures
version-name ordering across the four-level policy
downloader against a local socket server: redirect following, monotonic progress, oversized response, connection dying mid-file
the six-hour gate for every caller, the minutes reported to the user, and banner dismissal hiding only the notice for that release

release_tools.note: includes the manifest generator's schema, URLs and rejection cases

fdroid.updater_code: absent (no GithubUpdater, ReleaseFetch, ReleaseManifestParser, PackageInstalls or UpdateInstallReceiver in any dex)

not_verified: PackageInstaller install path on a device or emulator: this machine has no /dev/kvm
STATUS_PENDING_USER_ACTION confirmation dialog and the post-install restart
a download of a real published release from GitHub (tests use a local HTTP server)
behaviour behind captive portals, proxies or per-OEM installer prompts
the settings banner and row rendered on a screen; no emulator is available
review_fixes: a manual check obeys the same six-hour interval as the foreground hint and an attempt is recorded before the request, so a failed fetch or parse spends it too
dismissing a release hides only its banner; the update stays available in Settings and a manual check surfaces it again
installer verdicts reach the live row through a process-local flow, and the preferences copy is reconciled on foreground entry for a process that was killed mid-install
